items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: And my father was a musician and my earliest memories are of the downstairs jam session.

ctx.x: It’s interesting to speculate if you would have been doing this without your father’s influence? Do you think that that was — how significant was that for you?

It was very important. It was very important. I’m not sure what would have — how I would have come along if I hadn’t been born into my family, my existing family. And my father was a musician and my earliest memories are of the downstairs jam session. We lived in a two story house and I was awake, and I guess I must have been four years old or something. And toddled downstairs and they would be going at it. And it would be the middle of the night and you know, and the musicians would all be playing there and…

playing. And then if they weren’t the records would be playing. But the music was just almost constantly going. So I heard a lot of music and there wasn’t any television, no kid was sitting in front of a television because there wasn’t any television yet as I was growing up. I think personally it was a blessing to be born before television. It was a great advantage. I was born before — I woke up in front of the Victrola you know. And the instruments, and they were playing. And I heard a lot of music. So if I had…
